subject: Custody of secrets and data-residency language for private/on-prem deployments
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily@finstream.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finstream.com, procure@finstream.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on secrets custody & cross-border language for private deploy

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Security and procurement had a few follow-ups for us to sign off on private deployment (VPC/on-prem):

1) Customer-managed keys: we need confirmation on whether we can deploy with BYOK using our HSM and have Redwood never hold unencrypted model cache/keys. Is there an architecture diagram you can share showing where keys are in the flow?

2) Data egress: for EU-origin data we need contractual language that there will be no outbound transfer of raw customer data off the VPC unless we explicitly authorize it. We also need to know what subprocessors (infra partners) Redwood will use when supporting private deployments.

3) Audit access: what level of access will Redwood ops have for troubleshooting? Timestamped access logs and justifications for access would be required.

I've attached our initial DPA comments and a short checklist. Can your security and legal teams confirm feasibility and any lift for our infra team?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of Cloud Security, Finstream Capital

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on secrets custody & cross-border language for private deploy

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (product/security lead) and Neha (legal) so we can respond with specifics. High level:

- BYOK is supported for Private (VPC/on-prem). We have two supported modes: local HSM/BYOK where the customer controls root keys and a Redwood-side ephemeral wrapping key for runtime (Redwood never persists unwrapped keys), or a customer-managed Cloud KMS with strict IAM policies and no key export.
- For data residency, we support configurations that keep all customer data on the VPC and do not route logs or payloads through Redwood-hosted networks. We can contractually restrict egress and specify acceptable subprocessors.
- Ops access: we offer an audited, just-in-time access model. Accesss requires approval, and sessions are logged with reason. We can provide an access playbook for incident response.

I'll ask Karthik and Neha to attach the flow diagram and a proposed DPA clause set. Proposed next step: a 30-min call next Tue to walk the infra team through the key flow.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on secrets custody & cross-border language for private deploy

Emily/Team — quick technical notes from Product/Infra: we support two primary patterns for secrets and runtime keys: 

1) BYOHSM (bring your own HSM): customer HSM generates and stores the root key. The inference runtime performs local envelope encryption; the HSM performs unwrap/wrap operations via direct VPC network calls. Redwood does not have export capability. This is the strongest model for regulatory requirements (no key material leaves customer HSM).

2) Customer-managed KMS (cloud provider): customer KMS holds keys, Redwood uses a short-lived service principal over a private peering link. Keys never exported; we do get encrypted artifacts and ephemeral wrapping keys for the process but do not persist plaintext.

Operationally:
- We can operate in a zero-egress mode: control plane lives in a customer-managed VPC; support access is limited to a bastion-less remote runbook that requires customer approval.
- Subprocessors: for private deployments we typically only use (a) the cloud provider where the VPC runs and (b) our professional services partner Nimbus Cloud Services for initial onboarding (they have limited access and are bound by subcontractor DPA). I attached an exportable subprocessor list for procurement.

I'll be on the Tue call to demo the key handshake and access logs.

— Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: subprocessor-list-2027-05.csv]

From: Emily Zhang <emily@finstream.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: security@finstream.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on secrets custody & cross-border language for private deploy

Thanks Karthik — the BYOHSM option sounds promising. A couple follow-ups from security team: 

- Can you confirm whether runtime process memory ever includes unencrypted customer plaintext (e.g., model cache or inference inputs) in a way that could be paged out to disk on the host? We need guarantees or mitigations (seccomp, tmpfs, mlock).
- For subprocessors: Nimbus is fine for onboarding but we need a clause limiting their access window and requiring tokenized, time-limited credentials and a statement that they cannot export logs offsite.

Would Neha be able to provide redline language for the DPA covering these points? Also interested in your suggestion for SCCs or equivalent for EU transfers if we decide to run in an EU region.

— Emily

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Emily Zhang <emily@finstream.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on secrets custody & cross-border language for private deploy

Hi Emily,

Attached is a proposed redline for the DPA that:
- Adds a BYOK/BYOHSM exhibit outlining responsibilities (customer key custody, Redwood runtime obligations, and no-key-export guarantees).
- Introduces a limited-subprocessor clause: onboarding-only access (max 72 hours per engagement) for professional services with pre-approval from customer and required attestations.
- Specifies no-evidence-of-egress: Redwood must not transfer raw customer payloads off the customer VPC unless explicitly authorized and must list permitted operational metadata that may be shared (e.g., anonymized telemetry for performance).
- Adds an appendix for EU transfers: SCCs will be attached when relevant; for EU-hosted private deployments we recommend local-only control plane or a contract clause mandating data residency and no cross-border replication.

I also included proposed language for just-in-time ops access and audit log retention (90 days by default, extendable on request). Let me know if your legal/procurement want a tracked changes copy and a short call to walk through the clauses.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-dpa-draft-v2.pdf]

Emily — thanks for the rapid review. To keep procurement moving, proposed immediate next steps:

1) Procurement/Legal: review Neha's redline and confirm any specific wording on subprocessor time windows and audit retention by Thu this week.
2) Infra call (30 min): Tue 2027-05-31 09:00 PT — Karthik will demo BYOHSM handshake and memory hardening controls.
3) Tech checklist: Redwood to surface a short runbook describing: supported HSM types, network peering requirements, and a sample access request flow.

If that works, I will send a calendar invite and a short deck. Appreciate the collaboration — we aim to make Private deployments meet strict custody and residency needs with minimal procurement friction.

Best,
Vanessa
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
